title: Psychological mechanisms of change in the interdisciplinary multimodal treatment of pain disorders of the musculoskeletal system.
summary: Pain is widespread in Europe, affecting many people physically, psychologically and socially. Musculoskeletal pain, such as chronic back pain, is particularly common. Multimodal treatment approaches have been shown to be beneficial, but not all patients benefit equally. Which treatment factors are effective for whom and why is not yet fully understood. To answer this question, this study investigates psychological factors in the treatment of musculoskeletal pain disorders. The treatment consists of a 4-week outpatient, interdisciplinary and multimodal group program. The aim is to record and examine the effectiveness and possible mechanisms of change using questionnaires and objective tests. It is expected that physical and psychological well-being will improve after treatment compared to a waiting list phase. It is also expected that the psychological variables "self-efficacy" and "catastrophizing" will improve during the treatment phase and that the influence of the treatment on the treatment outcome (pain perception) will be mediated by these variables.
conditions: People with chronic pain in the musculoskeletal system. The following diagnoses, among others, can be assigned as main diagnoses:	F45.41, M54.4, M54.5, M53.1, M25.50, M25.55, M53.0, M54.6, M25.56, M54.2, M25.51, M51.1, M54.84, M54.87, M25.57, M77.0, M79.67, M16.2, F45.0

interventions.name: Waiting period (at least 2 weeks) and then 4 weeks of interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy in an outpatient clinic. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
People with chronic pain in the musculoskeletal system requiring interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy, previous outpatient treatment methods that have not been successful or have only been successful in the short term, written consent to participate in the study, sufficient knowledge of German and ability to understand and process the questionnaires and instruction material.
Exclusion criteria:
Participation in other studies, lack of group compatibility, inadequate physical capacity for the physical exercise program content, physical or mental illnesses that hinder therapy (e.g. significant internal illnesses or psychotic symptoms), clear conflict of interest between requesting a pension and alleviating symptoms, serious organic cause of pain (e.g. tumor, fracture, inflammation), pregnancy.
